trends.name: Iran Escalation & Oil Market Shock
trends.summary: Trump's hardline Iran rhetoric triggered immediate market reaction: oil surged past $110/barrel (+13%) with Chevron +2.9% and Exxon +3.2%, while Mag 7 stocks plummeted. Iran claims 7M citizens ready for conflict and is rebuilding drone capabilities via covert networks. Energy markets pricing in Strait of Hormuz disruption risk despite Goldman Sachs noting modern economies are less oil-shock sensitive than 1970s.

trends.name: Tech Sell-Off & Mag 7 Reversal
trends.summary: All seven mega-cap tech stocks declined sharply on Iran escalation fears: Nvidia -2.7%, Tesla -2.4%, Meta -2.4%, Alphabet -2.3%, Amazon -2.2%, Microsoft -1.3%, Apple -1%. Market rotation away from growth stocks into oil/energy suggests heightened risk-off sentiment and potential intermediate-term weakness in high-multiple tech positions.

trends.name: US Trade Deficit Widens & Export Surprise
trends.summary: February US trade deficit expanded to -$57.3B (vs -$54.5B prior, -$59.4B est), marking deterioration despite expectations. However, exports surged +4.2% M/M (vs -2.3% est) while imports jumped +4.3% (vs -0.2% est), signaling strong domestic demand but widening structural imbalances. Relevant to Trump tariff debate and dollar strength narratives.

trends.name: March CPI Inflation Report Preview
trends.summary: Investors bracing for potentially 'red-hot' March CPI report that could shock markets and reshape Fed rate-cut expectations. Rising oil prices, energy emergency in Philippines, and supply-chain tensions suggest inflationary pressures building. Market pricing shows high sensitivity to this data point as pivot indicator for monetary policy.

trends.name: Jobless Claims Mixed Signals
trends.summary: Initial jobless claims came in better than expected at 202K (vs 212K est), but continuing claims ticked up to 1.84M (vs 1.83M est, 1.82M prior). Mixed labor market signal suggests cooling employment growth without outright weakness, supporting soft-landing narrative but with deteriorating trend.

trends.name: Tesla Delivery Miss & EV Headwinds
trends.summary: Tesla reported 358K Q1 deliveries, down 14% Q/Q, signaling demand challenges and margin pressure. Stock down -2.4% on Iran concerns. Contrasts with Stellantis-backed Leapmotor exceeding 100K EVs quarterly. Suggests competitive EV market intensifying and Tesla's pricing/demand dynamics deteriorating.

trends.name: Private Credit Redemption Stress & Liquidity
trends.summary: Blue Owl capping private credit fund redemptions at 5% after steep request levels signals liquidity stress in alternative credit markets. Institutional investors seeking to exit high-yield private debt positions at a time of rising rates and macro uncertainty, indicating potential credit market vulnerability.

trends.name: Corporate Layoffs & Remote Work Policies
trends.summary: Oracle's mass email layoffs signal normalization of remote terminations across tech/finance sectors ('mass layoffs by email might be the new norm'). Citi requiring Paris/Frankfurt staff to work remotely post-bombing threat. Reflects cost-cutting and security concerns reshaping corporate employment culture.

trends.name: AI Infrastructure & Semiconductor Opportunity
trends.summary: Intel positioned as 'underdog to AI CPU comeback leader,' signaling investor thesis shift toward diversified AI chip competition beyond Nvidia. Reflects broader recognition that AI capex cycle benefits multiple semiconductor players, not just dominant leaders. Relevant to chip sector rotation.

trends.name: Dividend & Income Portfolio Strategies
trends.summary: Investors targeting $60K+ in growing dividends through SCHD core portfolios and BDC-heavy income strategies. Reflects shift toward yield-seeking behavior in higher-rate environment. Elevated dividend focus suggests risk-averse positioning and income generation priority over capital appreciation.

trends.name: Pharmaceutical/Healthcare: GLP-1 & Weight Loss
trends.summary: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill outperforming Lilly's oral GLP-1 in head-to-head trials, reshaping competitive dynamics in $100B+ weight-loss market. America's new weight-loss pill approval adds to secular trend. Significant for pharma valuations and healthcare sector rotation.

trends.name: Stock Market Correction & Valuation Reset
trends.summary: S&P 500 potentially bottoming by May with 6,000 cited as correction floor. Multiple analysts discussing 'fresh money' opportunities and contrarian valuations. Reflects broader debate about market cycle timing and whether current weakness creates entry points or signals deeper reversal.
